title: Trofie with Cashew and Pecorino Pesto
summary: Homemade basil pesto with toasted cashews and Pecorino Romano, tossed off the heat with trofie so it stays bright green.

steps.text: Pick the basil, discarding the thick stems but keeping the very thin, tender ones: you want about 95 g usable basil. Wash it and dry it very thoroughly.
Toast the cashews lightly in a dry pan for {timer:2-3}, then let them cool completely. This is optional, but it gives the cashews more nuttiness.
Blend or process the cashews and the garlic first. Add the basil and pulse briefly.
Add the Pecorino, then the olive oil gradually, pulsing only until smooth. Do not blend continuously for long: the heat darkens the basil and dulls the flavour.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water. Keep at least 150 g of the pasta water before draining.

Do not cook the pesto. Put the drained pasta in a bowl, or in the pan off the heat, add the pesto and about 60 g of the pasta water, and toss vigorously. Add more water gradually until the pesto turns creamy and coats the pasta.
Taste before adding any salt: the Pecorino and the salted pasta water already bring a lot.

tips: Basil is sold with its stems, so buy 130-150 g to end up with 95 g of leaves and tender stems.
Trofie are the best match: the twists hold the pesto. Linguine is my second choice; trenette, fusilli or spaghetti also work.
With all Pecorino and no Parmesan, make the pesto without salt and taste it first. It is stronger and saltier than Parmesan.
Use 100-150 g pasta water, as needed.
